text:
ellie (PM): ok team — I'm consolidating the visibility roadmap for Q2 focused on: dashboards, tracing hooks, cost breakdown, and error analytics. need quick alignment on scope & launch criteria. :spiral_calendar:

miguel (eng-runtime): quick note — tracing hooks add CPU + network overhead per request. we should quantify perf hits before committing. can we gate by sampling config?@sam?

sam (eng-sre): sampling is standard, +1 to instrument sampling knobs. also want SLO guardrails: if tail lat increases > 5% for 5m during rollout, auto-disable hooks for that deployment. ops-bot: automatic rollback rule templated below.

ops-bot: rollback-rule: {"metric":"p95_latency","window":"5m","threshold":"+5%","action":"disable_tracing_hooks"}

jia (obs-ux): for dashboards I propose two graduated surfaces: 1) Quick Overview (cost + error trends) — default home tile. 2) Deep Investigate (trace list + waterfall + raw span viewer) — behind a feature flag for early access. UX wants to avoid cluttering the console for new users.

frank (data): to power cost breakdown we'll need token-level attribution + route metadata. sampling complicates attribution accuracy — recommend hybrid approach: full-attribution for a subset of requests (1%-5%) + aggregated heuristics for the rest. also flag: embeddings/call types need separate cost models.

anya (cust-succ): customer asks we've collected: large SaaS client wants per-route cost URLs and automated alerts when a route exceeds expected monthly spend. another customer wants trace linking between frontend request id and model invocation id. both are blockers for early enterprise adoption.

ellie (PM): good. propose we split into three milestones: A) telemetry primitives + cost API (must-have), B) quick dashboards + basic trace hooks (canary-only), C) deep trace viewer + alerts + per-route billing export (enterprise GA).

miguel (eng-runtime): implementation note — primitives take ~3 sprints: token attribution pipeline, id propagation header, and low-overhead hook. can we reduce scope for B to only sampled traces + precomputed waterfall? that cuts runtime changes.

sam (eng-sre): rollout plan: canary in prod for 2 weeks with 0.5% traffic, measure p50/p95/p99 + error delta + cost delta. acceptance: no increase in p99 > 3% and errors not above baseline. if either fails, roll back. also need a playbook for customers on how to opt in/out.

jia (obs-ux): acceptance for dashboards: quick tile load < 1s for overview, drill latency < 2s for first render (sampled traces). show cost attribution confidence score when sampling is active.

ellie (PM): launch criteria (suggested):
- primitives: token attribution, request_id propagation, metrics emitted to prometheus and events to kinesis.
- canary: sampling enabled, dashboards visible to canary tenants, no more than 3% p99 regression.
- GA: per-route billing export available, alerts in console, trace viewer with span-level search.

frank (data): question on telemetry retention: how long do we keep raw spans for deep debugging? storing 30 days raw spans is expensive. propose: 7 days raw, 30 days aggregated metrics, and long-tail trace fetch via S3 cold storage.

anya (cust-succ): customers will push for 30d raw. we should offer a paid retention add-on and default to 7d to control costs. include pricing tier notes in the spec.

miguel (eng-runtime): cost tradeoffs: sampling reduces storage + CPU ~80% but degrades attribution. moving heavy processing off the hot path (batch enrichment) helps. quantization/compression for spans gives 2-3x storage reduction.

ellie (PM): open questions to resolve before FRD:
- exact sampling defaults and UX for changing them
- retention tiers + pricing language for sales
- canary thresholds and automation (ops-bot rule set)
- data access controls and PII redaction in spans

jia (obs-ux): I'll mock up the overview + investigate flows tomorrow and include sampling/retention tooltips.

sam (eng-sre): I'll draft the canary playbook and the ops-bot rule templates.

miguel (eng-runtime): I'll size the runtime changes and a simplified B-scope design (sampled-only trace viewer).

frank (data): I'll outline the attribution pipeline and retention-cost estimate with ballpark numbers.

anya (cust-succ): I'll surface the pricing-add-on ask to AE team and collect exact customer SLAs.

ellie (PM): great — thanks. next steps: sync tomorrow 10am PT to finalize FRD scope. pinned deliverables: FRD draft, canary playbook, UX mock, cost estimate. please drop blockers in this thread before EOD. :+1:
